rules.statement: Give exactly one of `observations` and `market_absence`. In `observations` each `kind` (bid, offer, indicative_talk) appears at most once; a bid is not above the offer and both carry the same `as_of_text` date.

Each quoted observation cites a page of a third_party source that holds its quote. `level_text` is a decimal numeral above 0 and at most 200, with no leading zero and at most four decimal places, occurring in the quote, and for a bid or offer labelled with that kind in the quote; an `indicative_talk` level is never one the quote labels bid or offer. A bid or offer needs `as_of_text` as a Month D, YYYY date occurring in the quote; `as_of_text` of indicative_talk may be null.

To use a quote listed in the context, submit the observation with its `kind` and its `context_row` (a listed row id), with `source_id`, `locator`, `quote` and `level_text` empty and `as_of_text` null; the `kind` must be the listed row's kind and the row must be listed, or the row is refused. All `context_row` observations of one submission name rows of the same facility. A context bid and offer are the two listed rows of one context quote (same facility and date), never one from the context and one from a sheet. Context market evidence is built by Python: cite it only by its row id in `context_row`, never with the `context` source as a `source_id`.

`instrument.name` occurs in `instrument.quote`. `terms.maturity` gives exactly one of `date_text` (a Month D, YYYY date occurring in its quote, after the quotation date) and `absence`. `terms.margin` and `terms.amortisation` each give exactly one of their text (`bps_text`, `value_text`, a numeral of at most three integer digits and four decimals, no leading zero, occurring once in its own quote) and `absence`, and the amortisation value is zero. `terms.reference_rate.name` occurs in its quote, and it gives exactly one of `level` (its `percent_text` occurring in the level's own quote, with no leading zero and at most three integer digits and four decimals) and `absence`.
Give exactly one of `recovery` and `recovery_absence`; `recovery.percent_text` is a numeral at least 0 and below 100 with at most two decimals and no leading zero.

Each `technicals` row has an `aspect` from quote_quality, trading_activity, talk_versus_quote and rating, each at most once, and a `category` from Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation and Insufficient Information. `limitation` is given for Insufficient Information and only for it, and a Documentary Fact has at least one `basis` quote on its page.

Every analyst text (`summary.text`, `technicals` text and limitation, `recovery.rationale`, `instrument.name`, `reference_rate.name` and every absence `reason` and `follow_up`) is nonblank, has no digit, and uses none of the words buy, sell, overweight, underweight, recommend, cheap, undervalued, overvalued, outperform or attractive; `summary.text` has no reference.

Read with `read_pages` every page you cite, and before you give `market_absence` or an `absence` for a term, run `search_pack` for it; an absence claim with no recorded search is refused. (`recovery_absence` is not an absence claim of this kind.)
Do not write Python's pinned-recovery line in a `technicals` limitation, in any case or spacing; Python adds that line when a recovery is pinned.
Rows from the context are Python's; refer to them by row id; never copy their figures.
